refuted_claims.claim: 'ALIENRPG.EVCriticalInjuries is JSON null in BOTH cn.json and zh-tw.json... Foundry's Localization#localize returns the key string for a non-string value, so actor.mjs:1812 calls game.tables.getName("ALIENRPG.EVCriticalInjuries") then falls back to the English name.'
refuted_claims.why_wrong: The stated mechanism is wrong. Foundry does NOT return the key for a non-string value; it falls through to the English _fallback dictionary first and only returns the raw stringId if the fallback is ALSO not a string. Since en.json defines the key as the string 'EV - Critical Injuries', localize() returns that English string. So actor.mjs:1812's first getName() call already receives the correct table name and the `||` fallback never fires. The null is fully transparent at runtime, not a case of a raw key leaking into a document lookup. The report's characterization of the failure path is inverted.

refuted_claims.claim: Four hardcoded_sites entries treat templates/active-effect/{config-duration,details,targeted-condition-prompt}.hbs as LIVE i18n surface: 'foreign-namespace i18n key (renders as raw key in EVERY language)' for 6 DRAW_STEEL.* keys, plus 6 EFFECT.* keys, with the fix 'lang/cn.json CAN define a DRAW_STEEL block'.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: None of these templates is ever loaded, so nothing renders as a raw key and a DRAW_STEEL block in cn.json is wasted work. The sheet that would render two of them, AlienRPGActiveEffectConfig (registered at alienrpg.mjs:228-229 as THE ActiveEffect sheet), points its `details` and `duration` PARTS at `systems/alienrpglates/sheets/active-effect/...` — a path that is doubly broken: no system id `alienrpglates` exists (only `alienrpg`), and no `sheets/active-effect/` subpath exists (the files are at `templates/active-effect/`). It is a botched find-and-replace of `alienrpg/temp`+`lates`. The third file, targeted-condition-prompt.hbs, is referenced only from a commented-out import of a .mjs that does not exist. The report inspected these files but never checked reachability, and in doing so missed the actual defect: the system's active-effect config sheet is broken.
refuted_claims.evidence: module/sheets/active-effect-config.mjs:21 `template: "systems/alienrpglates/sheets/active-effect/details.hbs"`, :24 `template: "systems/alienrpglates/sheets/active-effect/config-duration.hbs"`. `ls <data>/systems/` returns only: README.txt, alienrpg, crucible, dnd5e, pf2e, universal-tabletop-system — no `alienrpglates`. `ls templates/` shows no `sheets/` dir; actual files are templates/active-effect/{config-duration,details,targeted-condition-prompt}.hbs. Registration confirmed at module/alienrpg.mjs:228-229. `grep -rn targeted-condition-prompt module/ templates/` returns only module/documents/active-effect.mjs:1, a commented-out import.

refuted_claims.claim: Scope statement: '62 .mjs under module/ (20,024 lines)' presented as the complete module-JS scan, and hardcoded_sites contains no entry from any .js file.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: module/ contains 62 .mjs AND 12 .js files (5,428 additional lines) that the report never scanned. Two of those .js files are LIVE in the ES-module import graph reachable from the system.json esmodule entry, and both contain user-visible hardcoded English. The report's 'Scope scanned' line therefore understates the surface and the hardcoded_sites list is incomplete by construction.
refuted_claims.evidence: `find module -type f | sed 's/.*\.//' | sort | uniq -c` -> 1 hbs, 12 js, 62 mjs. Import-graph walk from module/alienrpg.mjs (following both `import ... from` and `export ... from` barrels) yields 62 live files of which two are .js: module/apps/update.js (imported at module/apps/init.mjs:1, called at init.mjs:62) and module/devmsg.js (imported at module/alienrpg.mjs:11, called at module/alienrpg.mjs:308).

refuted_claims.claim: 'switch(testArray[3]) on localize(\'ALIENRPG.Yes\')+\' \' / +\', -1 \' / +\', -2 \'' — the flagship CRITICAL COUPLING finding, offered as the exact strings a translator must keep in lockstep.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: The dashes are transcribed as ASCII hyphen-minus (U+002D). The actual source uses EN DASH (U+2013). Anyone building the lockstep translation or a matching Babele crit table from the report's strings will produce cases that can never match, silently losing the cFatal=true branches. In a finding the report itself flags as 'MOST IMPORTANT', the literal bytes are the whole deliverable.
refuted_claims.evidence: module/documents/actor.mjs:1906 and :1912 — hexdump of the non-ASCII char returns 0x2013 ('–'), not 0x2D. Lines read: `case game.i18n.localize("ALIENRPG.Yes") + ", –1 ":` and `... + ", –2 ":`. Also note the report cites 'actor.mjs:1955 healTime switch' for ALIENRPG.None; the None case is actually at actor.mjs:1924 (switch spans 1922-1941).

refuted_claims.claim: 'HTML TAG LOSS: 0. All 34 cn values containing markup have a tag multiset identical to en.'
refuted_claims.why_wrong: The conclusion (zero tag loss) is correct and reproduces, but the count is wrong: there are 26 markup-bearing values, not 34. A 30% error in a number presented under a 'COUNTS VERIFIED' banner.
refuted_claims.evidence: Recomputed on flattened lang/cn.json and lang/en.json with tag regex `<[^>]+>`: cn values containing markup = 26; en values containing markup = 26; overlap = 26; tag-multiset mismatches = 0.

refuted_claims.claim: '494 distinct ALIENRPG/TYPES/ACTOR/ITEM keys are referenced statically. 68 are missing from cn; another 98 exist in cn but are still English. So 166 of 494 live keys (34%) render English today.' and '34 keys are referenced but do NOT exist in en.json either.'
refuted_claims.why_wrong: Only the 68 reproduces exactly. Scanning the live import graph plus all 101 templates I get 487 distinct referenced keys (not 494), 94 byte-identical-to-en (not 98), 162 rendering English (not 166), and 35 referenced-but-absent-from-en (not 34). The direction and magnitude are right (~33% vs the claimed 34%) but the specific figures are not reproducible, so they should not be quoted as verified counts. Separately, the sentence promising '13 genuinely broken' raw keys then enumerates 15.
refuted_claims.evidence: Scan over the 62-file live import graph + 79 templates/*.hbs + 21 templates/*.html + module/helpers/alienprgSettings.hbs, regex `["'`]((?:ALIENRPG|TYPES|ACTOR|ITEM)\.[A-Za-z0-9_.\-/ ]*)["'`]`, comment lines stripped: 487 distinct core keys; referenced-and-in-en-but-missing-from-cn = 68; referenced-in-cn-byte-identical-to-en = 94; referenced-but-not-in-en = 35.

verdict: Roughly 85% of this report is solid and directly buildable; the lang-file half is excellent and the module half has real gaps. Everything I could recompute in lang/*.json reproduced exactly: 590/511/511 key counts, 93 missing, 140 byte-identical, 14 orphans, 162-of-511 no-CJK, the 22-key reconciliation (14 orphans + 6 reworded TYPES.* + ShipPanic9 whitespace + 1 null), placeholder loss = 0 with exactly 2 placeholder-bearing en keys, zero HTML tag-multiset loss, and the entire zh-tw sibling analysis (342 identical / 169 differing / 157 S-T-only / 12 substantive, including the cinematic='CINEMA' and CrewGunner leading-space examples). The cn quality critique is the strongest part — I spot-checked ~50 of the stale_or_wrong entries against the file and every one was accurate, including the marquee failures (仅限通用汽车, 守望先锋, 选择消防员, 图纸颜色设置, 重新启动计划) and the terminology-inconsistency clusters. The crit-injury coupling finding is real and correctly reasoned: cn.json genuinely translates None/OneRound/OneTurn/OneShift/OneDay while leaving Yes/Permanent/Shift English, so healTime does fall through to 0. Treat the following as unsafe: (1) the four active-effect template entries are dead surface — those templates never load because active-effect-config.mjs:21,24 point at the non-existent `systems/alienrpglates/...`, so skip the DRAW_STEEL/EFFECT work and instead file the broken path as a bug; (2) the EVCriticalInjuries null mechanism is described backwards — Foundry's localize falls through to the English _fallback, it does not return the key; (3) copy the en-dash (U+2013) from actor.mjs:1906/1912 rather than the report's ASCII hyphens before building any lockstep crit table; (4) re-derive the 494/98/166/34-key cross-check figures yourself (I get 487/94/162/35) — only the 68 is exact. Before scoping the runtime-patch module, add the seven missed items: the two unscanned live .js files (devmsg.js 'Alien RPG News', update.js dialog), the alienrpgct.* raw keys, the four creature-header data-labels, the Dice So Nice labels, {MISSING_CREW}, and — most consequentially for a Babele-based project — the Adventure-name and Journal-name lookup traps, which belong in the report's 'hard traps' section and are missing from it.
